records.name: Dashboard
records.description: What changed today across Vitruvian Manager: volatility's biggest movers, the topics rising and falling in the briefings' headlines, the next votes and summits, the markets, and what changed in the latest month of fighting UCDP has published, each line opening the one thing it names, over every module and submodule.

records.name: Global Headline Tracker
records.description: Any country's last 24 hours of news on a map, with daily, weekly, monthly and yearly archives of its top stories in the same view.

records.name: Geopolitical Volatility
records.description: A daily 0–100 index of conflict, political escalation, unrest, economic disruption and cross-border spread for every country, from GDELT, for one day or a period of days. Compare up to four countries.

records.name: Realtime Battlefield
records.description: Every armed conflict this year, grouped into wars, with plain-English briefings, a monthly archive (one month or a period of months) and related coverage. UCDP data, refreshed monthly.

records.name: National Analysis
records.description: Every country's PESTLE pressures, plus how it is governed, how often its leaders change and how much conflict it has seen. 41 indicators; compare up to four countries.

records.name: Month by Month
records.description: Each month, for every war VM follows (countries once UCDP's per-country figures are taken in): more deaths recorded, fewer, or no large change against the three months before, by one stated rule from UCDP's figures, each mark with its figures, period, evidence and confidence. With the month's bulletin, a watch list of the next 30 days' votes and summits, and a year strip for each War Focus war.

records.name: Political Atlas
records.description: Who holds power across 78 countries now: executives, legislatures, courts, elections, policies and challenges. Refreshed monthly.

records.name: Realtime Calendar
records.description: Upcoming elections, referendums and summits, plus the last six months of political events: new leaders, inaugurations and resignations, coups, wars and ceasefires, protests and strikes, parliamentary votes, court rulings, sanctions and party contests. Month or year view, any country or just the ones you highlight.

records.name: Highbrowse
records.description: The day's and the week's news across the four briefings: the biggest stories and topics, what each briefing covers most, the stories they share and how the political press spreads across five positions, with one search across all four by words, briefing, date and topic, and each topic's share of the stories this week against the weeks before.

records.name: Political Briefing
records.description: The top stories across fifty publishers, ten each from the far left, left, centre, right and far right, and each position's own top stories; then follow your topics side by side. Hard news only by default.

records.name: Scientific Briefing
records.description: New papers and news from the major journals and science desks (Nature, Science, Cell, PNAS, PRL and more), with a toggle for physics, chemistry, biology, earth & environment, and astronomy & space.

records.name: Economics Briefing
records.description: Economics news and scholarly articles from 50 feeds: NBER and CEPR working papers, the top journals, the BIS, ECB, Fed and Bank of England, VoxEU, Brookings and other think tanks, and the FT, Economist and Bloomberg, with a toggle by field (macro, monetary policy, trade, labour, development, finance, public finance, energy).

records.name: Digital Briefing
records.description: New papers and news on AI, computing, cybersecurity, chips, networks, quantum computing, data and digital policy, from the major journals, preprint servers, labs and technology desks, with a toggle by field.

records.name: Daily Synopsis
records.description: Each day's major political stories, those at least three of the Political Briefing's publishers from more than one side ran, with their 5 Sided Analysis: the outlets' own headlines laid out from far left to far right. A short digest and comparison written by an AI model (Claude) are added only when they pass VM's rules, and are labelled as such; no person checks them. A day is never rewritten once it has passed.

records.name: Master Index
records.description: Every person, place, war, party, idea, scientist and discovery in Vitruvian Manager. Filter with Boolean tag queries (e.g. Realist + American + "Political science") and jump to everywhere each one appears across the suite.

records.name: Political Retrospective
records.description: Move through the years from 1926 to today, or set a period of years with the timeline's two handles: historical borders, who was in charge of each country, and the key political events of every year, with Wikipedia links.

records.name: Retrospective Battlefield
records.description: Move through the years from 1926 to 2025, or set a period of years with the timeline's two handles, to see wars from 1926 and, from 1946, every armed conflict in UCDP/PRIO's record on a historical map, with sides, intensity where a source codes it, and Wikipedia links.

records.name: War Focus
records.description: The major wars of the last hundred years month by month: the states on each side and those wholly occupied, on a map with a timeline of months (one month, or a period with its two handles), battles, casualties and key facts, in the style of Ollie Bye's history-by-day videos.

records.name: Kardashev Tracker
records.description: Which empires and countries controlled what share of humanity's energy capture from 2000 BC to today, after Ian Morris, with humanity's Kardashev rating century by century, or the two ends of a period compared.

records.name: Historical Calendar
records.description: Political history from 1980 to today in one calendar: elections and referendums, new leaders and resignations, coups, wars and ceasefires, summits, protests, court rulings and more, each with a plain-English account.

records.name: Learning · Politics
records.description: The political spectrum through its leaders and thinkers: far left, left, centre, right (conservatism and market liberalism) and far right, and Mearsheimer and the Realists, a school of its own outside the left-to-right line, with quizzes.

records.name: OSINT Dashboard
records.description: An investigator's workbench for open sources: search across engines and archives, domains, company and sanctions records, event monitoring and image checks, with a case notebook that grades every source. Plus a Software Cookbook and a Kit Guide.

records.name: SIGINT Dashboard
records.description: Receive-only signals monitoring: aircraft (ADS-B), ships (AIS), satellites, LoRa mesh, GNSS interference and space weather from public feeds or your own receivers, plus a Software Cookbook and a Hardware Guide for hobbyists.

records.name: GEOINT & IMINT Dashboard
records.description: Geospatial and imagery intelligence: daily satellite imagery and night lights with before/after comparison, active fires, terrain, OpenStreetMap features, measuring and sun/shadow tools for geolocation and chronolocation. Plus a Software Cookbook and a Hardware Guide.

records.name: Intel Training
records.description: Courses in intelligence tradecraft, each with quizzes and capstone exercises: OSINT (the intelligence cycle, sources, search, verification, records, analysis and the law), SIGINT (radio fundamentals and lawful, receive-only monitoring of aircraft, ships, satellites and the spectrum) and GEOINT & IMINT (satellite imagery, geolocation, chronolocation and measurement), and how to use Vitruvian Manager’s dashboards for each.

records.name: Market Monitor
records.description: Markets now: indices, rates, FX, commodities and crypto, movers, news, ticker pages and the Hype Tracker of tickers suddenly talked about or traded far more than usual.

records.name: Auto Trader
records.description: Three parts in one. Omni Trade: Trading 212, Alpaca, Interactive Brokers, Coinbase and Kraken in one ledger, with balances, positions, orders, rules, risk limits, the kill switch and an MCP connection for AI agents (private). Investor Impersonator: what members of Congress (including Nancy Pelosi) and famous investors such as Buffett, Burry and Ackman are buying and selling, from STOCK Act and SEC 13F filings, and an agent that mirrors any of them or trades in their style. Algo Trader: trading agents that follow a ruleset, such as Double Agent (stocks that double within hours) and Hype Rider (the Hype Tracker), each simulating first with its own pot under the shared risk limits (private).

records.name: Learning · Finance & Economics
records.description: Two introductory courses: Finance, with worked examples and quizzes, and Economics, taught through Smith, Marx, Keynes, Mises, Friedman and Werner.

records.name: Invention Timeline
records.description: Move through history, or set a period with the timeline's two handles, to see key scientific breakthroughs appear where they happened, tagged by discipline, discoverer and institution, and linked to the Master Index.

records.name: Data Analytics
records.description: Explore and chart Vitruvian Manager’s own data: pick any dataset from the catalogue, filter, group and aggregate it, draw charts in Vitruvian Manager’s style, export them, and hand the analysis to an AI assistant.

records.name: Omni-Map
records.description: Dated borders and the battles VM holds on one map, opened at the right place and years from a name in Neo Book, each value with its source and its date as recorded; a view saves as a citable bundle. Borders for every year Cliopatria v0.2.1 covers, 3400 BC to AD 2024.

records.name: Integration Hub
records.description: Connect AI assistants and plugins to Vitruvian Manager: a catalogue of every dataset, a read-only MCP server, a JSON API, feeds and calendars, and setup guides for Claude and other tools.

records.name: IoT Connect
records.description: Command your own smart bulbs, speakers, TVs and the EZCast receiver from one page through the Vitruvian Manager bridge, with Hermes Messenger to identify devices and walk through their pairing, an MQTT and Sparkplug link to a unified namespace, and your phone as the remote.

records.name: Political Events
records.description: Documentaries on political turning points, starting with the Russian Revolutions of 1917, the Partition of India and the Revolutions of 1989.

records.name: Political Figures
records.description: Lives in power, told with maps, timelines, portraits and their own words: Winston Churchill, Franklin D. Roosevelt and Deng Xiaoping to begin with.

records.name: Political Parties
records.description: How parties rise, rule and adapt, starting with the Chinese Communist Party, Mexico's Institutional Revolutionary Party and Japan's Liberal Democratic Party.

records.name: Wars
records.description: Wars from their causes to their aftermath, starting with the Second World War in Europe and Africa, the Korean War and the Vietnam War, with maps that follow War Focus month by month.

records.name: Geopolitical Events
records.description: Moments that reshaped the world order, starting with the Cuban Missile Crisis, the end of the Soviet Union and the end of empire in Africa.

records.name: Great Thinkers
records.description: Short introductions, in three parts with a short quiz, to the great minds Vitruvian Manager draws on, starting with Niccolò Machiavelli, Adam Smith and Karl Marx, each linking to the thinker's own book where Bibliotheca's shelf holds one.

records.name: Neo Book
records.description: Public-domain books read on screen, from Thucydides and Machiavelli to Gibbon, Smith, Darwin, Clausewitz, Marx and the Austrian economists. Every term the Master Index knows is highlighted, a bar lists the terms on screen, a pane beside the text opens the Master Index entry or the other screens for the book's era, and the AR Reader reads the book aloud.
